Rabid Seals

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Over the last two years there have been several reports of divers and surfers being attacked by seals in the waters around Cape Town. The latest was on 26th May in Muizenberg. 3 surfers were attacked by a young seal who “hunted” them. Biting through the wetsuit of one surfer and latching onto his board. He manged to fight him off by punching it, but it went on to attack 2 more surfers. Dion Bing was on the beach at the time and recorded the event on his surf report.




Summary:
On 4th January last year a young seal attacked a child in the water on Clifton Beach and an visiting America actress. People put this behaviour down to a bacterial infection of the brain caused by red tide bloom called Domic acid poisoning. It causes swelling around the brain and heart. But the last 4 seals the SPCA tested have tested positive for rabies.
It’s an alarming finding as there is no cure for rabies in either humans or animals. If you get bitten on an extremity and immediately have a rabies vaccination you have a chance but if you get bitten on the face or upper body that’s a different matter.


Further information:
There has been an outbreak of rabies in animals in the Western Cape over the last few weeks and subsequent drive to inoculate as many animals as possible. A few weeks back a couple of dogs attacked a seal at Big Bay. NSPCA believe that seal must have contracted rabies from the dogs or other mammal like mongees? Those dogs were traced an vacinnated
In domestic animals when they have rabies they get aggressive and in wild animals they have the opposite reaction, they become “tame” Whats tricky about seals is that they display both behaviour. In the sea they are calm but on land if cornered attack- so spotting a rabid seal it tricky. Seals are curious and playful and surfers often see them- but its rather terrifying when they attack.
Rabies is extremely easy to catch, you don’t have to be bitten- you can just get a lick from a rabid animal. On Monday 10th of June 2024 a child was bitten in Hout Bay harbour by one of the seals. The SPCA will start vaccinating all the seals in Hout Bay harbour- and that’s a relatively easy task because the have tagged those seals. A couple of months ago they captured the habituated seals in Hout Bay and took them far up the West Coast- but they swam back! Kalk Bay harbour also has a number of resident seals, but these ones aren’t tagged so that will be another mission.
Rabies in seals is bizarre and very scary- the other know case is in California where they believed a bat eared fox bit a seal.
“Rabies is an acute, progressive encephalomyelitis caused by lyssaviruses. This zoonosis occurs worldwide in mammals, with dogs, bats, and wild carnivores as the principal reservoirs. Typical clinical signs include acute behavioral changes and progressive paralysis.” Rabies alliance

Script:


Opening sequence
Simon” A little seal came at me at high speed and it lurched onto my back backside - but it kept coming at me.
Keith: The seal chased me an attacked me about 5 times
Jami: You don't know if you're going to die in that moment or if you're going to come out with a leg or without a leg.
LINK: Seals are curious and playful - often popping up amongst people in the water - but in the last few years there has been a surge in unprovoked attacks on people – and they can do serious damage.
VO: Swimmers, surfers, kayakers and even people walking on the beach have been attacked –
often so severely they have been hospitalised.
VO: We joined a group of experts to Duiker Island off Hout Bay. For the last few years they have been trying to figure out, this extreme aggression in seals.
VO: Three weeks ago, they tested a dead seal for rabies for the first time - and to their shock it was positive.
Upsound Greg on boat Clip 47 “ We cant get onto the island and test all the seals”
VO Greg Oelofse is from the City of Cape Town’s Coastal Management. And because they cant get onto the island, they’re relying on the expertise of people used to diving with seals.
Gregg: they're helping us in mapping out that that's an aggressive seal. This is a normal behavior. So we can start putting together what we essentially call a case definition. If it's behaving in this way, then it's a likely candidate for rabies.
VO: For the last 7 years Jami Marnitz has spent 100s of hours in the water with seals and experienced some horrifying attacks
Jami - A tag is when they nip your arm and swim away and attack is when they go for your fins and work their way up your body and thrashes you around and it does not stop
Erin “and you have had that 3 times”
Jami So the seal definitely follows you, um, when it's in this attack mode…., once you're on the boat, you're not actually safe. …. I've had my boats, pontoons being ripped by a seal.
VO: So common has this behaviour now become, that divers have a name for it.
upsound
Jami: A crazy or rogue seal has cherry red, kind of evil looking eyes. They most of the time have a lot of foam that comes out of their mouths. 00:14:22:15 The seal can't really stay underneath the water, so it kind of floats. And they do this kind of meerkat pose on top of the surface, kind of darting at you and chasing at you with, with purpose.
Link: This outbreak of rabies in seals around Cape Town has come as a major shock- there is only one other reported case in the world in 1981 in Norway. Marine biologists, vets, coastal authorities are putting their heads together trying to figure it out
VO: Rabies is a deadly disease. It’s a virus that infects the central nervous system and when symptoms appear, victims die within a matter of days. It’s spread through saliva and scratches from an infected animal. Symptoms are aggression, hyperactivity, frothing at the mouth, and paralysis of the throat muscles causing a fear of water. But, it can take months - even years - for symptoms to show.

VO To date - there are eight confirmed cases - including a baby seal that attacked 5 surfers off Muizenberg in False Bay last month.
Simon Aaron was one of them.
Simon” A little seal came at me at high speed and it lurched onto my back
Simon: It jumped onto my backside area and bite me in the in, in the buttocks area. And then it climbed up my back and, uh, bit me in the lower back area. ….I shook it off and it went flying off….. it then kept coming back at me.
VO After being fought off, the seal turned on another surfer, Keith Kelly.

Keith: The seal was climbing on the back of my board, two foot from the back of the seal was biting at the back trying to jump onto the board. …I came into the beach and I turned around and I saw the seals swimming away.
VO: Despite their injuries, Simon and Keith continued surfing. There’ve been no reported cases of rabies in seals in the world for the last 40 years, so it was the last thing on their minds.
At around the same time, a clue as to what was happening emerged in nearby Noordhoek.
A dog that had bitten its owner and a veterinary nurse was diagnosed with rabies. According to Dr Karyn Levy the first case in Cape Town
Karyn: He was foaming at the mouth. He was biting the upholstery in the car. There was saliva and blood everywhere. He'd bitten the owner. He was manic in his expression. Um, my vet and my handler sedated him, twice he was still very very aggressive
VO: Is it possible these incidents provide insight into the spread of a deadly virus on land… and at sea?
Karyn After extensive questioning from all of us and also from the state vet. She was adamant that her four dogs had not been in any dog fights but she did say they had had fights with seals on the beach
VO: The seal that first tested positive for rabies had been attacked by dogs on a beach in Blouberg, towards the West Coast. And it seems this case had a similar explanation.
Jaco Pietersen, from the SPCA, has rescued many seals attacked by both dogs and people.
Erin: Do we know if the dogs are giving the seals rabies, or are the seals giving the dogs rabies?
Jaco: At this stage it's all very new to us all. And we don't know yet how the rabies are spreading amongst the seals. It could be from seals attacking one another, or it could be from land animals that are biting the seals. So at this point in time it is all just speculation.
Erin: Now that rabies has been found in seals will you be testing all the Cape fur seals for this?
Jaco: It's not possible to test live animals, and therefore, it makes it extra difficult to locate the source and to find seals that are positive.
VO: Seals are popular with tourists in Hout Bay - and bites are common. So, as a precaution, the SPCA will vaccinate seals at all harbours.
Jami We've been advised that anybody who's been bitten or attacked in the last year needs to go for their rabies vaccinations.
VO: since her last attack Jami hasn’t been back in the water. Knowing they might have rabies - has added to her trauma.

Jami -It's like something from a zombie apocalypse 00:09:47:24 -It's extremely painful. You're trying to keep your head above water, and they're so powerful that they do pull you underneath the water

Upsound
VO: With over 2 million seals along our coastline, travelling vast distances , how extensive is the infection? The conservation group Sea Search is going back through 120 samples collected since 2021 - and coming up with some alarming results. They found rabies from August 2023 and as far east as Plettenberg bay. And it's not only seals- otters have also been attacking people
Greg . 00.03.09.00 we're doing our very best to understand as quickly as we can. We're concerned around the potential for transfer of rabies from seals to things like Cape otter or mongoose or similar and other coastal wildlife

VO: Right now there are more questions than answers – next month scientists from across the globe are flying into Cape Town to compare their research findings.
Jaco: We also don't want to cause distress amongst the public. All we are asking is stay away from seals. And if you come across the seal on the beach, keep your distance. If you are concerned about the seals wellbeing rather phone, the SPCA or the City of Cape Town to and we will send someone.

She was adamant that her four dogs had not been in any dog fights but she did say they had had fights with seals on the beach VO: The seal that first tested positive for rabies had been attacked by dogs on a beach in Blouberg, towards the West Coast. And it seems this case had a similar explanation. Jaco Pietersen, from the SPCA, has rescued many seals attacked by both dogs and people. Erin: Do we know if the dogs are giving the seals rabies, or are the seals giving the dogs rabies? Jaco: At this stage it's all very new to us all. And we don't know yet how the rabies are spreading amongst the seals. It could be from seals attacking one another, or it could be from land animals that are biting the seals. So at this point in time it is all just speculation. Erin: Now that rabies has been found in seals will you be testing all the Cape fur seals for this? Jaco: It's not possible to test live animals, and therefore, it makes it extra difficult to locate the source and to find seals that are positive. VO: Seals are popular with tourists in Hout Bay - and bites are common. So, as a precaution, the SPCA will vaccinate seals at all harbours. Jami We've been advised that anybody who's been bitten or attacked in the last year needs to go for their rabies vaccinations. VO: since her last attack Jami hasn’t been back in the water. Knowing they might have rabies - has added to her trauma. Jami -It's like something from a zombie apocalypse 00:09:47:24 -It's extremely painful. You're trying to keep your head above water, and they're so powerful that they do pull you underneath the water Upsound VO: With over 2 million seals along our coastline, travelling vast distances , how extensive is the infection? The conservation group Sea Search is going back through 120 samples collected since 2021 - and coming up with some alarming results. They found rabies from August 2023 and as far east as Plettenberg bay. And it's not only seals- otters have also been attacking people Greg . 00.03.09.00 we're doing our very best to understand as quickly as we can. We're concerned around the potential for transfer of rabies from seals to things like Cape otter or mongoose or similar and other coastal wildlife VO: Right now there are more questions than answers – next month scientists from across the globe are flying into Cape Town to compare their research findings. Jaco: We also don't want to cause distress amongst the public. All we are asking is stay away from seals. And if you come across the seal on the beach, keep your distance. If you are concerned about the seals wellbeing rather phone, the SPCA or the City of Cape Town to and we will send someone.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Over the last two years there have been several reports of divers and surfers being attacked by seals in the waters around Cape Town. The latest was on 26th May in Muizenberg. 3 surfers were attacked by a young seal who “hunted” them. Biting through the wetsuit of one surfer and latching onto his board. He manged to fight him off by punching it, but it went on to attack 2 more surfers. Dion Bing was on the beach at the time and recorded the event on his surf report.
metadata.Summary: On 4th January last year a young seal attacked a child in the water on Clifton Beach and an visiting America actress. People put this behaviour down to a bacterial infection of the brain caused by red tide bloom called Domic acid poisoning. It causes swelling around the brain and heart. But the last 4 seals the SPCA tested have tested positive for rabies. It’s an alarming finding as there is no cure for rabies in either humans or animals. If you get bitten on an extremity and immediately have a rabies vaccination you have a chance but if you get bitten on the face or upper body that’s a different matter.
metadata.Further information: There has been an outbreak of rabies in animals in the Western Cape over the last few weeks and subsequent drive to inoculate as many animals as possible. A few weeks back a couple of dogs attacked a seal at Big Bay. NSPCA believe that seal must have contracted rabies from the dogs or other mammal like mongees? Those dogs were traced an vacinnated In domestic animals when they have rabies they get aggressive and in wild animals they have the opposite reaction, they become “tame” Whats tricky about seals is that they display both behaviour. In the sea they are calm but on land if cornered attack- so spotting a rabid seal it tricky. Seals are curious and playful and surfers often see them- but its rather terrifying when they attack. Rabies is extremely easy to catch, you don’t have to be bitten- you can just get a lick from a rabid animal. On Monday 10th of June 2024 a child was bitten in Hout Bay harbour by one of the seals. The SPCA will start vaccinating all the seals in Hout Bay harbour- and that’s a relatively easy task because the have tagged those seals. A couple of months ago they captured the habituated seals in Hout Bay and took them far up the West Coast- but they swam back! Kalk Bay harbour also has a number of resident seals, but these ones aren’t tagged so that will be another mission. Rabies in seals is bizarre and very scary- the other know case is in California where they believed a bat eared fox bit a seal. “Rabies is an acute, progressive encephalomyelitis caused by lyssaviruses. This zoonosis occurs worldwide in mammals, with dogs, bats, and wild carnivores as the principal reservoirs. Typical clinical signs include acute behavioral changes and progressive paralysis.” Rabies alliance
